federalism.title: Senate divisions
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, s. 22 (four divisions of 24 senators, with Newfoundland and the territories added)
federalism.detail: The Senate is built from four equal divisions of provinces. A region that spans two divisions has no seat count that follows from the text. 9 regions span two or more divisions: Maritime Coastal, Rivière Saint-Maurice, Southern Rivière Betsiamites, Boreal Shield, Northern Quebec.

federalism.title: The 7/50 amending formula
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1982, s. 38(1) (resolutions of two-thirds of the provinces with at least half the population)
federalism.detail: Two-thirds of the units, holding at least half the population, can amend the constitution. With a different number of units, the threshold is a different set of people. Two-thirds of 26 units is 18. The 18 largest hold 94% of the people; the 18 smallest hold 33%.

federalism.title: Equalization
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1982, s. 36(2) (equalization payments so provinces can provide reasonably comparable services at reasonably comparable levels of taxation)
federalism.detail: Equalization measures fiscal capacity per person against the national average. Redrawing the units moves the average and changes who is below it. 13 of 26 regions fall below the set's GDP per person; Maritime Coastal is furthest below it. GDP here is an allocation, so read this as a shape, not a payment.

federalism.title: Quebec's asymmetry
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, ss. 94, 133 and Constitution Act, 1982, s. 59 (Quebec's civil law, its legislature and its language guarantees)
federalism.detail: Quebec's civil law, language guarantees and opt-outs attach to Quebec as a unit. A set that cuts Quebec into pieces has to say which piece they attach to. Quebec is spread over 7 regions, and 7 of them also hold ground in another province.

federalism.title: Territorial status
federalism.citation: Northwest Territories Act, S.C. 2014, c. 2, s. 2; Yukon Act, S.C. 2002, c. 7; Nunavut Act, S.C. 1993, c. 28 (territories are created by Parliament, not by the constitutional amending formula)
federalism.detail: The territories exist by federal statute and can be changed by Parliament alone; provinces cannot. A region joining territory to province mixes the two. 3 regions join territory to province: Taiga Shield, Northern Ontario, Arctic Coast–Islands.

federalism.title: The senatorial floor on Commons seats
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, s. 51A (no province has fewer Commons seats than senators)
federalism.detail: The floor keeps small provinces over-represented in the Commons. It is written for provinces as they are; new units of very different size change who it protects. The smallest region holds 0.1% of the set's people, under one seat's worth, so the floor would carry it.
